description: The plot illustrates the relationship between step number and accuracy for two experiments, labeled Ex1 and Ex2. The x-axis is labeled “Step” and has a linear scale ranging from 0 to 60000, with tick labels at intervals of 10000. The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy (Next Token Prediction)” and has a linear scale ranging from 0.10 to 0.40, with tick labels at intervals of 0.05. A blue line, representing Ex1 Accuracy, begins at (0, 0.10) and increases sharply to approximately (10000, 0.43), then plateaus, remaining at approximately 0.43 through (60000, 0.43). A teal line, representing Ex2 Accuracy, starts at (0, 0.24) and rises to approximately (20000, 0.30), after which it remains relatively constant at approximately 0.30 through (60000, 0.30). Both lines are solid and are marked with circular data points.
caption_used: Accuracy comparison of Ex1 and Ex2 during the Embedding and LM Head training stage. The plot demonstrates that Ex1 Accuracy consistently exceeds Ex2 Accuracy across all steps, with Ex1 reaching a plateau of approximately 0.45 by step 10,000 and remaining stable thereafter. In contrast, Ex2 Accuracy shows a slower rate of increase, plateauing at approximately 0.30 by step 20,000 and remaining steady through step 60,000. Both lines exhibit an initial sharp rise, but Ex1 demonstrates a significantly higher rate of improvement compared to Ex2 in the early stages.
